name: archive_extract
description: Extract the members of a zip, tar (plain, gzip, bzip2, xz or zstd), 7z (through the 7z program) or single-file gzip/bzip2/xz/zstd archive into a NEW private directory, bounded and safe against hostile input. Format is read from the bytes. Only member CONTENT is written: a symlink, hard link, device node or FIFO is recorded with its target and never created, nothing lands outside the output directory (files are created exclusively through directory descriptors; an absolute path, a drive letter or '..' is rendered harmless and flagged), and nothing is executed. Every member is one row of members.jsonl in archive order (n is the number the archive-members recipe gives it) with its exact name bytes (name_b64), type, declared and written sizes, the times as stored with their zone said, flags, status and the path it was written to; two members with one name are two files; an encrypted member is counted, never skipped silently and never opened; a compression method this build cannot read is 'unsupported'. A name shaped like a token is withheld from every output channel and kept in withheld-names.jsonl (0600). A member is written as <path>.partial and takes its name only when its size and CRC match what the archive declared; a member that stops, fails or mismatches stays .partial and its row says why. A digest or CRC of a member shorter than 128 bytes is not written. Budgets: max_total_bytes, max_member_bytes, max_members, max_ratio (default 1000), max_depth and max_seconds; a member-level budget skips or cuts that member and goes on, a global one stops the run, names it and gives next_index (run again with from_index and resume true to go on in the same out_dir, which writes a second manifest beside the first). A nested archive is named (looks_like), not opened; one call extracts one level. A gzip, bzip2 or xz tar is complete only when its whole stream has been read: after the tar's end blocks the rest of the decompressed stream and every further compressed stream are read, under the clock and the ratio budget, and must be zeros; a further tar header or other data, a trailer that does not match (the gzip CRC-32 or length) or a stream that does not end, bytes after the last stream that are not zero padding, or a rest the budget or the clock cut short make the answer partial, naming the offset (zstd tars are read as before). zstd needs Python 3.14 or the zstd program, else it is reported unsupported. RAR, CAB and ISO are refused by name. A 7z archive with encrypted headers cannot be listed and is refused. Not measured: the content of any member, the archive's authenticity, and whether the archive is the whole of what was acquired. Extracted bytes are evidence content and can hold credentials: when the member list shows credential stores, keys, tokens or browser profiles, run it as a job with secret_output true. The manifest does not force it: an archive of a whole case would make every output sensitive. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 15: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

path.description: The archive to extract (a file). Its format is read from its bytes, not its name.

out_dir.description: Directory to extract into (default: a new archive_extract-<id> directory beside the tool's other output). Must not already hold files unless resume is true. In a job it must lie under $OUT: give {OUT}/<name>.

resume.description: Go on in an out_dir an earlier run made (with from_index). Nothing already there is replaced; a second members.2.jsonl and receipt.2.json are written.

from_index.description: Start at this member number (default 0): the number a stopped run gave as next_index, and the n of the archive-members recipe.

max_total_bytes.description: Bytes written in all (default 8 GiB, at most 1 TiB); past it the run stops and names where to resume.

max_member_bytes.description: Bytes in one member (default 4 GiB); a longer member is cut, kept as .partial, and the run goes on.

max_members.description: Members handled in this run (default 200000, at most 5000000).

max_ratio.description: Expanded over packed (default 1000): per member for a zip (its directory gives each packed size); over the whole stream for a gzip, bzip2, xz or zstd file or tar, and for a 7z (its output over the archive's size); a plain tar stores its members. A sparse disk image compressed with xz or zstd can pass it; raise it for such an archive on purpose.

max_depth.description: Path components in a member name (default 64); a deeper member is skipped and recorded.

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds (default 1500, at most 1700); past it the run stops, and any running 7z is killed.

limit.description: Member rows in the inline page (default 50, at most 1000); members_file has every member.
